basis: The orphan claim survives, established by my own commands. `git grep -nE 'scoring' 06d9f8ce -- web ':!web/coverage' ':!web/package-lock.json'` returns empty — this is the decisive absence command, and because it covers all of web/ rather than only web/src it also disposes of the non-TS surfaces the run card warns the frontend map cannot see (vite.config.js, index.html, package.json scripts, playwright config, web/tests, web/scripts) and of the barrel-re-export path, since any `export * from './scoring'` would have matched. `git grep -nE '\b(ScoreCard|FACTOR_DISPLAY_NAMES|DataGap|Verdict|Factor)\b' 06d9f8ce -- web internal cmd` returns only the five declarations inside web/src/types/scoring.ts plus one unrelated same-name collision, internal/adapters/clients/dh/types.go:131 `Verdict string \`json:"verdict"\`` — a DH API field, not this module. I read the file (git show 06d9f8ce:web/src/types/scoring.ts): five declarations, snake_case fields (entity_id, engine_verdict, data_gaps, scored_at), and no Go counterpart, since internal/domain/scoring does not exist at the baseline.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: The defect is real; the severity is not. Four of the five declarations are TypeScript types, which are erased at compile time, and the fifth (FACTOR_DISPLAY_NAMES) is unreachable from the entry graph, so Vite never bundles the module. There is no runtime cost, no bundle weight, and no behavior at stake — the entire consequence is that a reader may believe a scoring contract exists. That is a low, not a medium. Deletion is still correct and the acceptance criteria prove it cleanly.

basis: Both sides re-read at the baseline rather than taken from the finding's quotation. git show 06d9f8ce:internal/domain/inventory/health_types.go:12-19 shows PortfolioHealth with six flat fields and no embedded struct, so there is no promoted delta field. git show 06d9f8ce:web/src/types/campaigns/analytics.ts:244-252 shows the TS mirror carrying realizedROIDelta and totalRecoveredDelta. The direction is as the finding states: TS models what Go never emits. `git grep -niE 'roidelta|recovereddelta|PortfolioDelta' 06d9f8ce -- internal cmd` exits 1 with no output, ruling out a differently-cased tag, a map literal, or string-built JSON anywhere in Go. I then closed the wrapper gap the finding does not address — a handler could add fields the domain struct lacks: internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/campaigns_finance.go:115-118 serializes *inventory.PortfolioHealth straight through serviceCall, wired at internal/adapters/httpserver/routes.go:182, and the frontend reads it unmodified via web/src/js/api/campaignAnalytics.ts:58-59 and web/src/react/queries/useCampaignQueries.ts:52-53. what_the_finding_got_wrong: One overstatement in the title. FreshnessLine is not dead — I read it at HeroStatsBar.tsx:211-224 and it is driven by asOfMs, returning null only when no timestamp exists; the delta parameter controls just the optional label span at :220. So the dead surface is the two DeltaChip renders (:89, :145) and one label span, not a whole component. This does not change the severity: the drift is real, three branches never fire, and a reviewer reading HeroStatsBar would reasonably believe the dashboard shows deltas that it cannot.

what_the_finding_got_wrong: The central consequence is wrong for four of the seven fields, and I found it only by widening the search beyond the finding's pathspec. `git grep -nE 'inHandCapitalCents|liquidationLossCents|ebayChannelMarginPct|inTransitUnsoldCount|inHandUnsoldCount|liquidationSaleCount|inTransitCapitalCents' 06d9f8ce -- .claude/skills/campaign-analysis` returns hits in api-cheatsheet.md:173-176 and field-semantics.md:192-210, the latter documenting `/api/portfolio/snapshot` -> `.health.campaigns[].inHandCapitalCents` as an aggregation source. The four in-hand/in-transit fields have a real, tracked-in-repo consumer that reads the JSON API directly rather than through the browser, so 'shipped over the wire on every portfolio-health response and discarded unread' is false for them. Separately, ebayChannelMarginPct is not inert on the Go side either: internal/domain/portfolio/suggestion_rules.go:271, :314, :315 branch on it. What actually remains is the narrow and still-valid defect: the TS mirror is an incomplete copy of the Go contract, which is debt under this repo's manual type-sync convention. Severity stays low — it is already the floor, and I could not lower it further. The controller should rewrite the consequence before ticketing, and should note the finding is `strong`, not `mechanical`, so it is not ticketable unqualified under the preamble's tiering.

basis: All four legs checked separately, since the finding fails if the tracked-in-git leg fails. Tracked: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 06d9f8ce -- web/coverage | wc -l` returns 51. Stale: `git log -1 --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short 06d9f8ce -- web/coverage` returns `84288a18 2026-03-25 Initial Commit`, so untouched for over four months. Not ignored: I read both ignore files in full rather than grepping. git show 06d9f8ce:.gitignore has no coverage entry — its only 'coverage' occurrence is the comment at :11 above the Go `*.out` rule — and git show 06d9f8ce:web/.gitignore lists node_modules, dist, logs, editors, env, test-results, playwright-report, screenshots and storybook, but no coverage directory. what_the_finding_got_wrong: One arithmetic conflation, immaterial to the conclusion. The report contains 35 source-file pages, of which 28 no longer exist and 7 still do.
